Star Field (experiments/star-field)

A WebGPU-first space-exploration scene — the Solar System plus notable Milky Way, Local-Group and cosmic-hierarchy objects (112 catalog bodies) — rendered as an orbiting chart with raycast selection, camera fly-to, a searchable 139k-record deep-field registry, lazy per-body dossiers and PNG screenshot download. Route: /star-field-experiment (canonical) plus a localized slug per supported locale; listed in the hamburger menu.

The chart's north star is honest geometry: every named object sits at its real galactic (l, b, distance) through gpos(); nothing is clustered for readability. Sizes compress in three documented distance tiers, the Solar System is a point-scale diagram inside the star field, and the whole galactic frame co-rotates so the Sun orbits the galactic centre as part of the disc — never a stationary exhibit.

Boot sequence

StarFieldEngine.init() → bootstrapStarField(s) — every async checkpoint re-checks s.disposed so a mid-boot destroy() can never half-attach listeners, and onReady fires exactly once (success or bail) so the loader can never stick.

sequenceDiagram participant Host as StarField.tsx participant Eng as starfield-engine participant Boot as bootstrap.ts participant GPU as renderer-setup participant Wrk as fill-worker/wasmPool Host->>Eng: init() Eng->>Boot: bootstrapStarField(s) Boot->>Boot: lazy import three + webgpu + tsl + OrbitControls Boot->>GPU: initStarRenderer(s, WebGPURenderer) GPU->>GPU: webglAllowed() gate alt gate fails GPU-->>Boot: false → bail (CSS fallback) else gate passes GPU->>GPU: WebGPU adapter probe alt adapter ok GPU->>GPU: WebGPURenderer + logarithmicDepthBuffer else probe/init fails GPU->>GPU: clone canvas → forceWebGL retry end end Boot->>Boot: setupStarCamera + loadStarTextures (progress 10→80) Boot->>Boot: setupStarScene + buildStarBodies (progress 84) Boot->>Boot: bindPicking + handleStarResize + warmUpShaders (92) Boot->>Boot: tickStar() — first frame (100, onReady) Boot->>Wrk: ensureStarCloud() — fire-and-forget Wrk->>Wrk: fetch HYG binary → wasm decode/fill → mount on MW disc Eng-->>Host: onReady → dismiss loader (or failed → CSS fallback)

Scale & coordinate model

The chart is a multi-scale diagram — 20 orders of magnitude separate Neptune's orbit from the observable universe, so distance compresses in three tiers while every direction stays astronomically true:

Tier Range Scale Contents
Galactic < 1 Mly 100 ly / unit MW disc (520 u), named stars, nebulae, dwarfs
Local Group 1–10 Mly 800 ly / unit M31 (~11.9k u), M33, Local Group shell
Cosmic > 10 Mly 20 000 ly / u Superclusters, observable-universe shell (46k u)
flowchart LR subgraph input["Author-time values"] LB["real galactic (l, b, d_ly)"] AU["AU-scale solar defs"] end LB --> CD["sfChartDist — piecewise<br/>galactic/local/cosmic tiers"] CD --> GP["sfGalacticPos — spherical→cartesian<br/>+ shared MW_TILT frame"] GP --> RID{"inside CO_ROTATE_R<br/>of the Sun?"} RID -->|"yes"| SPIN["parent onto mw.spinner<br/>(co-rotating rider)"] RID -->|"no"| WORLD["world-fixed node"] AU --> SHR["shrinkSolar × SOLAR_SCALE (0.002)<br/>Sun → 0.024 u ≪ Proxima's 0.042 u"] SHR --> RID

Key honesty invariants:

  • SOLAR_SCALE lands the Sun's drawn disc at 0.024 units — inside Proxima Centauri's true 0.042-unit distance, so no star renders inside the photosphere, and the whole solar tier (~0.23 u) sits inside the nearest stellar distances instead of claiming neighbourhood space.
  • Named-star markers are point lights, not spheres — galactic stars never resolve a disc at honest distances, so their luminous body is a filled glow sprite keyed to luminosity class; pickability comes from a radius-scaled invisible proxy (PICK_PROXY ×4), never geometry.
  • Nebulae/clusters carry honest extents (Ring Nebula 0.008 u, Tarantula 3.25 u) — sprites dissolve into the field under additive blending.
  • The stellar neighbourhood bubble is not a carved void: it is a sparse-dim underdensity (the real Local Bubble), no boundary shell.

Co-rotation

bodies-scene.ts mounts every node whose whole extent fits inside SF_SCALE.CO_ROTATE_R (800 u) of the Sun into the Milky Way disc's spinner — the galactic rider. The solar system, named stars, the deep-field cloud and disc members all orbit the galactic centre as one structure; only extragalactic/hierarchy objects stay world-fixed. def.spin for the MW is a slow geological drift (0.02 → ~44-minute core lap) with SF_SPIRAL.ROTOR_DIFF× differential inner-disc motion.

flowchart TB MW["milky-way spinner<br/>spin 0.02 + rotor ×1.6"] --> RIDER["galactic rider group"] RIDER --> SUN["solar tier (0.002×)"] RIDER --> NBS["named stars @ true (l,b,d)"] RIDER --> NEBS["nebulae/clusters"] RIDER --> CLD["deep-field 139k-star cloud"] RIDER --> SGR["sagittarius-a (disc centre, local frame)"] MW -.->|"world-fixed"| EXT["M31 · M33 · dwarfs · hierarchy shells"]

Floating origin

The rider parks the Sun ~6.7 M units out on its true 26.7 k-ly ring, so following any body dragged the camera into coordinates where float32 quantization visibly wobbles every mesh. followSelected (frame/camera.ts) instead pins the followed anchor at the world origin — it counter-translates a dedicated s.world group each frame while the camera itself stays put. Selection sets s.followId and repins synchronously before startFly, so the tween's track() resolves inside the pinned frame and only glides the local gap — a Moon↔Earth or Jupiter↔moon pick slides sideways rather than zooming out across the galactic span. flyHome rides the Sun anchor the same way (Overview frames the solar tier out to the Kuiper belt while the Sun keeps orbiting). The sun-light PointLight is reparented onto the Sun anchor so bodies stay lit wherever the pin lands.

Renderer contract

Same gate as the earth playground: webglAllowed() first (honours ?debug=webGLMode:fallback and real WebGL absence), WebGPU adapter probe, WebGL retry on a cloned canvas after a failed init (a poisoned context never recovers). Failure at any stage resolves init() with failed so the host swaps in the 2D starfield surface.

The chart spans a 2e7 near/far ratio (NEAR 0.01 → FAR 200 000) — far beyond linear 24-bit depth precision — so the renderer runs a logarithmic depth buffer, which keeps precision roughly uniform from planet specks to the observable-universe shell.

Every custom material is a TSL node material (three/tsl + MeshBasicNodeMaterial) — the fresnel-limb luminous shader, structure shell rims and the accretion disc are injected through the SFNodeDeps bundle. Classic GLSL ShaderMaterial does not compile under the node pipeline — new materials must be TSL.

Luminous composite per star — two regimes. Resolved solar-tier stars (the Sun): granulated procedural photosphere (sunspots/faculae by activity) → fresnel limb darkening → masked corona sprite (photosphere cutout, Hα eruption plumes) → annulus halo (eased multi-stop tail, transparent core so it never washes the disc). Galactic stars are point lights: no sphere mesh at all — an invisible pick proxy + a filled point-glow sprite sized by the authored luminosity radius, so a marker can never render as a planet-like ball next to a body it doesn't actually neighbour. Fly-to tweens track the anchor's live world position every frame (SFFly.track), so a selected body inside the rotating rider can't leave the camera landing where it was at arm time.

Earth — day/night, seasons, atmosphere

Bodies listed in s.dayNight carry a shared sun-direction vector that frame/updates.ts recomputes each frame from the Sun anchor's world position (works under the pinned frame). On Earth the vector drives three layers:

  • Night-lights gate (bodies/primitives.ts emissiveNode on a MeshStandardNodeMaterial): the city-light texture is multiplied by 1 − smoothstep(LO, HI, dot(worldNormal, sunDir)), so lights only burn below the terminator — a plain emissiveMap is unlit and would glow on the day side.
  • Seasons (bodies-scene.ts axis lock + frame/fx.ts tint): a counter-rotating lock group cancels the orbit pivot's Y-rotation on the tilt group, keeping the axis inertially fixed — the terminator sweeps real hemispheres over the year. The cycle warm↔ice surface tint keys off cos(pivot.y), so solstice/equinox fall out of the orbital phase rather than a wall-clock timer.
  • Atmosphere (makeAtmoShell): a fresnel-limb MeshBasicNodeMaterial shell one step past the cloud deck — bright scattering blue on the day limb, an amber dusk band through the terminator, dim deep blue on the night limb; opacity also thins where the air is unlit.
  • Near-Earth satellites (makeConstellation + constellation.id): the Starlink-class glint shell is a dossier-backed pick target — an invisible proxy bubble at the jittered outer radius registers the swarm's own node/anchor, so clicking the dot annulus opens the near-earth-satellites dossier while the proxy still loses to Earth's real mesh (and to the ISS bubble inside it) along the ray.
  • Near-field reach override (frame/updates.ts): swarm holders and rider shells carry userData[SF_USER_DETAIL_R] — an absolute camera distance that replaces the generic max(radius, orbit)·SCALE reach, so Earth's 44-unit orbit can't reveal the LEO shell beyond lunar range.
  • Comets (bodies/comet.ts, SF_KINDS.COMET): Halley rides a retrograde, steeply-inclined eccentric conic — an irregular coal-dark nucleus in an additive coma, with ion + dust tails each backed by a scrolling filament-gas sprite, all locked anti-sunward (tails live on center, where local +x always points away from the Sun). Tails ignite only inside a periapsis window (SF_COMET.ACTIVE_FRAC — sublimation ≈ 1/r² flux) and unmount entirely on the outer leg.
  • Plumes (bodies/plumes.ts): def.plumes vents spawn tapered cone jets + rising/fading puffs co-rotating with the surface — Enceladus' south-polar tiger-stripe geysers, Io's volcanic plumes — gated by dot(ventDir, sunDirLocal) so night-side vents dim.
  • Belts (bodies/belt.ts + bodies/belt-rocks.ts): selectable — an invisible RingGeometry proxy (SF_USER_PROXY, so real meshes on the ray still win) fills the annulus, and seeded hero rocks (stone/ carbon/hydrated/dust/ice/metal classes, irregular geometry, own Keplerian pivots) ride inside the particle disc and resolve the same body id through the parent chain.
  • Surface recipes (bodies/procedural/surface.ts + SF_SURFACES): untextured solid bodies get a seeded equirect canvas — def.surface pins rock/ice/gas/lava/ocean recipes per dossier climate (Proxima d lava crust, TRAPPIST-1e/f ocean + caps, 1h ice streaks); ASTEROID and COMET kinds join the cratered-rock club.
  • Dwarf-galaxy halos (galaxy.ts): elliptical dwarfs get a seeded elliptical star cloud plus a soft glowTex backing smudge at DWARF_HALO_SCALE, so distant dwarfs read as haze rather than sparse point dust.

Frame loop

tickStar self-reschedules via RAF; tickFrame is the catchable body. All per-frame work is synchronous — batch CPU work (spiral fills, binary decode, speckles, belt) routes through fill-worker.ts → wasmPool off-thread with bit-identical JS fallbacks.

flowchart LR RAF["RAF"] --> TICK["tickStar<br/>(throw → failed+fallback)"] TICK --> CAM["frame/camera — floating-origin pin,<br/>fly tween, follow, hints, controls"] TICK --> UPD["frame/updates — orbit/spin,<br/>satellites, LOD, day/night<br/>vectors, approach prefetch"] TICK --> FX["frame/fx — pulses, flares,<br/>seasonal tint, cloud fade,<br/>structure rims"] UPD --> REN["renderer.render"] FX --> REN REN --> RAF

Mobile layout (< 768px)

flowchart TB subgraph chrome["Bottom chrome — decluttered"] TOG["Explore toggle (bottom-left)"] ACT["Actions (bottom-right, stacked)"] end subgraph sheets["Capped sheets — max-height 50dvh"] NAV["Nav drawer — auto-closes on select;<br/>scale disclaimer lives at its foot"] PAN["Dossier panel — slides up over scene"] end TOG --> NAV NAV -->|"pick a body"| PAN DESK["Desktop-only: pinned disclaimer strip,<br/>gesture hint, side drawers"] -.->|"hidden"| chrome

On small screens the pinned disclaimer paragraph and the gesture hint are display:none — the disclaimer text moves inside the nav drawer's scroll (one gesture away), and the two sheets cap at half the viewport so the scene always keeps its upper half.

Registry (deep catalog)

public/data/registry/manifest.json + per-kind shards (star, exoplanet, dso) — 139k records. The nav drawer lists loaded records per kind with a 1 000-record "load more" step; a non-empty query hits searchRegistry across all shards. Registry ids resolve through registryWorldPos (heliocentric → rider frame) and fly at SF_STAR_CLOUD.FLY_OFFSET; dossiers synthesize from record fields with the locale's fact labels — no per-star JSON exists.

Accessibility contract

  • Navigator drawer: one semantic <button> per catalog body plus a registry search input and per-kind "load more" paging — the complete keyboard path that canvas picking can't provide.
  • Escape precedence: dossier panel first, drawer second.
  • aria-live="polite" HUD announces hover and selection names.
  • Pointer events cover mouse/touch/pen; click-vs-drag threshold keeps orbit drags from selecting.
  • prefers-reduced-motion → single static frame, no RAF loop.
  • Mobile sheets are real focusable chrome: nav toggle exposes aria-expanded/aria-controls, panel content is inert while closed.

Translations

translations/<loc>/pages/star-field (seeded in database.json for all 16 locales): title, systemBoot, hint, explore, group headings (solar, milkyWay, nebulae, galaxies, localGroup, hierarchy), screenshot, overview, loading, source, catalog, records, loadMore, searching, registry fact labels (magnitude, distance, spectralType, constellation, designation, hostStar, dsoType, discovery, redshift, coordinates, registry_*/_about), plus kind labels (star, planet, dwarfPlanet, moon, blackHole, system, nebula, galaxy, cluster, exoplanet, dso, dwarfGalaxy, structure, belt). APP.starField carries the nav label; slugs.starField the localized route; English ships in FALLBACK_PAGES for the pre-fetch window. Body dossier JSONs are per-locale with an English fallback (source-credited scientific prose).

Screenshots

engine/screenshot.ts re-renders the current frame, then canvas.toDataURL() → anchor download; tainted-canvas path falls back to toBlob + object URL. When both produce nothing, no download is attempted.

Tests

tests/starfield/ — component, render, boot, dossier, i18n and engine facade suites. tests/coverage/starfield/{component,engine,star}/ — tails for the arms the happy-path suites can't reach (mocked StarFieldEngine, mocked bootstrapStarField, mocked catalog, tag re-registration, zero-viewport resize, shader-warmup aborts, wasm-dispatch fallbacks, mid-flight disposal). Module gate: 100% statements/branches/functions/lines per file.
